page.layout: One page of text, running head at top with page number 240; main text in one column; faint show-through notes in the right margin (not transcribed as notes, as they are mirrored text from the facing page); no catchword; the text column ends with the line "priu" set at right.

main_text.p: amarulentam invidiam, nescio quid malignum de fraude trahit, quod non nisi obtortis oculis aspici potest. Quin huc etiam opprobrii contemptusque speciem ad acerbitatis summam accersit: Dum namque suorum decora clangit fublatâ tubâ, aut his imparia Exteris improperat, aut paribus insolenter obstrepit: Donec assidentium turba, diuturno jam lacessita fastidio, mordaces hinc inde regerit facetias, & tandem inter irridentium sibilos demittit confusum praeconem: Et verò si pretio isto aliquantus Patriæ veniret homnos, non essent detrectanda ludibria; Scomma est, quod illi emi tanto, & eodem nobiscum Patriam involvimus convitio: Gravitatem fastui, splendorem luxu vertunt interpretes peverfissimi. Ajunt comem illū, qui nobis prio priu

page.notes: Page is slightly skewed and the right edge is cut by the facing page; the final line "priu" is a catchword-like fragment at the right margin and is a partial line of the text (it reads "priu" continuing "prius"). Several words at the line ends are uncertain and the right-hand edge is shadowed; readings such as "homnos" and "Patriam" are as printed in the scan, with line-end damage possible. Faint mirrored text in the right margin was omitted as show-through.
